result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_regular()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if the graph is regular (all nodes have the same degree). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4498-L4560){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_regular() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A graph is regular if every node has the same degree. For directed graphs, this means all nodes have the same in-degree and the same out-degree (though in-degree and out-degree don't need to equal each other). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph is regular, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - empty graphs and single-node graphs are considered regular - cycles are 2-regular - complete graphs `K_n` are `(n-1)`-regular - for directed graphs, checks both in-degree and out-degree regularity ## Examples {.doc-examples} Every node in a cycle has exactly two neighbors, so cycles are always regular: ::: {#f89ed402 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_cycle_graph(5) graph.is_regular() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: A star's hub connects to every other node while each spoke connects only to the hub, so their degrees differ and the graph isn't regular: ::: {#22682e63 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_star_graph(4) graph.is_regular() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: In a complete graph, every node connects to all `n - 1` others, so all degrees match: ::: {#766a3f0c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() n = 5 for i in range(n): graph.add_node(label=f"n{i}") nodes = sorted(graph.get_node_ids()) for i in range(n): for j in range(i + 1, n): graph.add_edge(nodes[i], nodes[j]) graph.is_regular() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: :::
